target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):**

- `processes.ts` — after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners:
  ```ts
  const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
  child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  ```
- `http.ts` — identical guard after the guarded `spawn` in `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest`.

**Mutation-sensitive regression test** (`sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts`): it spies on `node:child_process` `spawn` to capture the real spawned child, then **deterministically emits `error` on the real `child.stdout` and `child.stderr`** for both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP path. It asserts each stream carries an `error` listener, that emitting the error does not throw, that the WebSocket bridge stays `OPEN`, and (process path) that the bridge still runs follow-up work.

Because emitting `error` on a stream with no `error` listener throws synchronously, removing either production listener makes the test fail — proving the test protects the exact fixed path.

**Diagnostic proof — fix present vs. removed:**

With the fix in place:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

With **both** `child.stdout.on("error", …)` / `child.stderr.on("error", …)` removed from `processes.ts` and `http.ts` (mutation), the same test fails on the real emitted stream errors:

```text
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > process bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors and keeps serving
 AssertionError: process stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > streaming HTTP bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors after headers
 AssertionError: http stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

**Sibling exec-server suites still green after the rebase:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs sandbox-exec-server.{http,lifecycle,json-rpc}.test.ts sandbox-exec-server.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The same no-op `error` listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
